notes: Summary: Auric is evaluating dedicated capacity to replace an in-house inference farm used for customer-facing ranking/chat. Primary drivers: predictable unit cost, tighter latency SLOs, and simplified ops (reduce infra headcount).
Workload profile: mix of reranking for search (burst-heavy, peak 3k qps), embeddings batch jobs (overnight), and chat assistant (low-latency p95 requirement).
Latency/Throughput targets: chat p95 <= 50ms; rerank p99 <= 120ms at 3k qps sustained bursts; embeddings throughput 200k vectors/hour overnight window.
Reserved capacity ask: evaluate 3 commit levels — conservative (30% util), baseline (55% util), aggressive (80% util). Finance wants model sensitivity to utilization +/-10%.

Cost modeling notes: SE ran per-GPU token unit economics using Redwood sample kernel picks. Key levers in model: batch size, KV cache hit rate, quantization (int8 vs fp16), and continuous batching efficiency.
Unit economics draft (from workshop):
- Conservative commit: 4x A100-class GPUs reserved — effective cost/token (est) $0.0009 for generation tokens at 40% utilization; cost/token for embeddings $0.00002 per vector.
- Baseline commit: 8x GPUs reserved — model shows $0.00045/token at 55% util with caching benefits on repeated prefixes; improves burst headroom with autoscale credits.
- Aggressive commit: 16x GPUs reserved — $0.00028/token at 80% util but marginal benefits diminish once KV cache hit rate > 70% (bound by model compute).
Observations from POC runs: tail-latency spikes tied to KV cache warm-up and inter-arrival variance. Redwood recommends warm-start policies and prefix caching to hit p95 targets.

SLA negotiation items raised by Auric legal/security: financial credits for sustained latency breaches, data residency clause for EU customers, right to audit, and minimum notice for maintenance windows. They requested a 99.9% availability SLA for dedicated pools.

Open technical questions: exact GPU SKU (A100 vs H100) mix for best price/perf on reranking; whether to use quantized model variants for chat to reduce cost without quality regressions; recommended autoscale burst pool sizing and cold-start mitigation.
Quote from Head of ML Ops: 'If we save 30–40% on unit cost with the same or better p95, we can justify the three-year commit.'
Procurement constraints: CFO prefers multi-year commit only if downside protection included (commit break clauses and utilization reconciliation).
Next recommended steps (from AE/SE):
1) Run 2-week POC with three reserved tiers (4/8/16 GPUs) instrumented for token-level cost, KV cache hit rate, and latency percentiles.
2) Produce final cost sensitivity workbook (drive:/Auric/Redwood/auric_redwood_pricing_model_v1.xlsx) with scenarios: QPS variance +/-25%, cache hit range 40–80%, quantization uplift tests.
3) Draft SLA with proposed credits schedule and maintenance windows; circulate to legal (target: 2026-04-01).
4) Security to confirm iso27001 artifacts; provide KMS integration plan and audit log retention options.

Blockers reiterated in call: finance needs full three-year TCO vs cloud; InfoSec wants third-party audit copies; product owner wants a guarded canary rollout plan to avoid model regressions in production.

cost_model_summary: Three-tier reserved plan. Conservative 4 GPUs -> higher cost/token but low commit risk. Baseline 8 GPUs -> best balance at expected load, shows 35–45% unit-cost reduction vs current self-hosted runbook. Aggressive 16 GPUs -> lowest unit cost but requires >70% sustained util to realize savings. Sensitivity to KV cache hit rate is high; +20% cache hit reduces effective token cost by 15–22% depending on workload.
